sections.title: Habit and range
sections.text: Coffea canephora, often called robusta, is an evergreen shrub or small tree native to tropical western and central Africa, about 4–8 m tall. Its leaves are opposite and thick, the white flowers are axillary, and ripe drupes turn red.

sections.title: Seeds and comparison
sections.text: The fruits usually contain two seeds, which are dried and roasted to make coffee. The species is cultivated in the tropics, often at lower elevations than C. arabica, though this is not an absolute distinction. The plate shows leaves, white flowers and red berries; visual differences between species can vary.
